subject: Degradation window carveout & monthly compensation mechanism
messages:
From: Kyle Reynolds <kyle.reynolds@veridian.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: sre@veridian.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: degradation window carveout & monthly credit approach

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the hosted pilot run last quarter — things are shaping up well. We have a situation on our side I wanted to surface early: our monthly end-of-cycle batch (large model re-encoding + analytics) generates extended sustained load on inference for a 2–5 hour window most nights during our month-end period. When this coincides with peak usage it can push P95 latency above our target and in some cases trigger an availability dip that would technically count against the SLA.

We have two asks and would like to see Redwood’s standard approach before we get legal involved:
- Can we get a defined "degradation window" carveout for scheduled batch windows that are notified in advance (we can provide a calendar CSV with the expected nights)?
- If a degradation window remains insufficient, what is Redwood’s proposed monthly compensation/remedy calculation (credits) tied to the impact? We prefer something predictable and capped rather than ad-hoc credits per incident.

I attached our batch calendar (veridian-batch-calendar.csv). For context, these windows are predictable (02:00–05:00 UTC typical) and we could accept limited throttling during those windows if it avoids broader outages.

Would appreciate a short draft proposal we can feed to procurement.

Thanks,
Kyle
Kyle Reynolds
Head of Ops, Veridian Health
ops@veridian.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Reynolds <kyle.reynolds@veridian.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: degradation window carveout & monthly credit approach

Hi Kyle — thanks for the clear note and the batch calendar. We can take a pragmatic approach that keeps your month-end jobs predictable while preserving service reliability for interactive traffic. High level proposal below; I attached a short definition doc and a sample remedy calculator for transparency.

Summary proposal (draft):
- Definition: A "Degradation Window" is a scheduled, customer-declared batch interval (start/end) during which Redwood may temporarily relax latency SLOs for affected routes. To qualify: customer must provide 14 days' advance notice for recurring windows, or 72 hours for limited ad-hoc windows, and label the windows in the Veridian calendar.
- Scope: Carveout applies only to explicit routes identified in the calendar. Interactive endpoints remain subject to standard uptime/latency SLOs.
- Limits: Up to 6 hours per declared window; up to 4 declared windows per calendar month without renegotiation. Any usage beyond that reverts to standard SLA measurement.
- Measurement: During a declared window, "availability" calculations exclude only minutes where latency exceeds P95 by >3x baseline AND total account QPS is dominated by declared batch traffic (our telemetry will determine). We will share the raw telemetry slice on request.
- Remedy / compensation: Monthly remedy will be an aggregated credit, calculated as a function of total minutes outside expected performance during non-carveout hours plus a small weighting for qualified degradation minutes inside declared windows. We propose a capped monthly credit equal to the lesser of: (A) 1.5% of the monthly invoice, or (B) the outcome of the attached remedy calculator (minutes-weighted). This provides predictability for both parties.

Next steps:
1) If you sign off on the principles above, we will generate an SLA amendment (DocuSign) that adds a "Degradation Window" clause and the remedy cap.
2) If Veridian prefers an alternative cap (e.g., flat dollar ceiling), tell us the target and we’ll test impact on our side.
3) We can run a one-month pilot where we allow 6 hours in the declared windows but meter the real-time impact to validate the measurement method.

Attachments: redwood-degradation-def.pdf, monthly-remedy-calculator.xlsx, redwood-sla-amendment-draft.docx

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk the numbers.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Reliability & Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: degradation window carveout & monthly credit approach — position and fallback

Ben/Laura — forwarding Veridian's ask and my draft reply. Key negotiating points I want aligned on before we send the DocuSign:

1) Capacity vs uptime: we should only allow carveout when telemetry shows the batch is the primary traffic cause (>65% of QPS). Otherwise the carveout is gaming. We can instrument that automatically.

2) Frequency and duration cap: I set 6 hours and 4 windows/month in the draft. We can relax to 8 hours or 6 windows if they commit to a higher monthly reservation (dedicated capacity) — use as an upsell lever.

3) Remedy cap: I proposed min(1.5% monthly invoice, calculator outcome). 1.5% buys us predictability and is defensible. If procurement pushes back, offer a two-tiered cap: 1.5% standard, 3% pilot month (one time) with telemetry review.

4) Inside-window weight: give them a reduced weighting for minutes inside declared windows (e.g., 0.25x the outside-window penalty). That keeps their predictability but still holds us accountable for severe regressions.

5) Legal language: ask Legal to add explicit notice requirements and a clause that carveouts don't apply to data plane incidents that affect other customers.

Asks for you both: please confirm the cap acceptability and whether we should tie extra carveout permission to a discounted dedicated commitment. If you approve, I’ll prepare the DocuSign amendment and an internal playbook for SRE to handle telemetry checks.

—Irene

Subject: Re: Request: degradation window carveout & monthly credit approach

Kyle — appreciate the quick turnaround on the calendar. We've coordinated internally and revised the draft to be conservative and transparent. Short version below; full amendment will be in DocuSign once you confirm.

Proposed amendment highlights (final draft):
- Qualification: Veridian declares windows in the shared calendar and provides 14 days' notice for recurring windows.
- Limits: Up to 6 hours per declared window, up to 4 declared windows per month.
- Measurement: During a declared window we will measure performance but apply a reduced weight to qualified degradation minutes (0.25x). A minute only counts as a "qualified degradation minute" if (a) P95 latency > 3x baseline AND (b) batch traffic accounts for >65% of total QPS for the account during that minute.
- Remedy calculation: Monthly aggregated remedy is computed via the attached calculator; however the monthly credit is capped at the lesser of (i) 1.5% of the monthly invoice, or (ii) the calculator result.
- Pilot option: If Veridian signs a 6-month dedicated commitment of reserved capacity at a negotiated uplift, we will increase allowance to 8 hours per window and up to 6 windows per month.

Ask from Veridian: Please reply with one of the following by EOD Friday so we can generate the SLA amendment in DocuSign:
A) Accept principles as-is (we'll send DocuSign).
B) Counter a different monthly cap (give % or flat-dollar target).
C) Request a call to walk the calculator (we'll schedule 20 min).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/REDWOOD-VERIDIAN-SLA-AMEND
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/VER-347

If we don't hear back we can open a short pilot where we apply the declared-window rule for one month without the cap change, purely for measurement.

Best,
